meta.agent: Agent K — Distractor Quality Score Review
meta.scope: 38 Domain E seeds (Pack C: 19, Pack D: 19)
meta.methodology: DQS 6-dimension scoring per CAQS v1.0: Plausibility, Distinctness, Trap Coverage, Balance, Domain Alignment, Psychometric Quality
meta.note: Choice quality (learner-facing options) is scored separately from explanation quality (feedback text). DL-026 empty explanation slots penalize explanation quality only — the choice text is evaluated independently.

globalFindings.rotation_group_pattern: All 38 seeds are the unique QID in 5-item rotation groups. The 4 companion items per group are Archived (question_state: 'Archived') and share identical stems with different company names + positionally rotated choices. This means every seed's distractors are shared with its group-mates.

dl026_prevalence.description: DL-026 = empty ExplanationWrong field at non-CorrectChoice position. Learner sees no feedback for that distractor.
dl026_prevalence.impact: ~16 of 38 seeds (42%) have at least one empty distractor explanation slot

explanation_quality_assessment.choice_specific_substantive: ~60% of non-empty explanation slots have genuine, choice-specific text referencing appropriate accounting/control principles
explanation_quality_assessment.generic_boilerplate: ~10% of slots use generic 'This option reflects a misunderstanding...' template text (DL-013 variant)
explanation_quality_assessment.cross_domain_citation_error: Pack D ED-056-060 rotation group clones cite 'ASC 715 (Retirement Benefits)' as authority for internal control cost-benefit questions — wrong domain

cma_trap_coverage.overall: Low to moderate. Most distractors test basic concept confusion (e.g., COSO component vs. COSO component) rather than documented CMA exam traps.
cma_trap_coverage.best_examples: EC-021 (segregation duties application), EC-022 (preventive vs. detective), EC-023 (access deprovisioning), ED-028 (COSO component discrimination), ED-064 (vendor master risk identification)
cma_trap_coverage.worst_examples: EC-008 group (COSO identification — all distractors are other well-known frameworks, obvious by elimination for any CMAnominee)

P1-EC-004.stem: Emberton assigns one employee to authorize purchases, another to record them, and a third to reconcile the vendor accounts. What internal control concept does this reflect?

choices.A: Segregation of duties, reducing the risk of undetected errors or fraud
choices.B: Cost-benefit analysis, which weighs control costs against benefits
choices.C: Management override, which bypasses controls
choices.D: Risk acceptance, which tolerates a known exposure

explanationSlots.EW_B: Cost-benefit analysis may influence control design, but it is not the control concept shown by separating authorization, recording, and reconciliation.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Management override is a bypass of controls by someone with authority; here, duties are separated rather than bypassed.

P1-EC-004.assessment: Choices are decent — B, C, D are all legitimate COSO/control concepts that could confuse a novice. D is the weakest distractor (risk acceptance is one step removed from segregation). One empty explanation slot (EW_D) is a DL-026 gap. ExplanationCorrect references COSO segregation principles implicitly. Moderate quality.
P1-EC-004.certification_readiness: Needs DL-026 fix (EW_D needs text). Choices acceptable.

P1-EC-008.stem: Hearthstone evaluates its internal control system using a widely recognized framework consisting of five integrated components. What framework is this?

choices.A: The Six Sigma DMAIC framework
choices.B: The Balanced Scorecard framework
choices.C: The Theory of Constraints framework
choices.D: The COSO Internal Control - Integrated Framework

explanationSlots.EW_B: The Balanced Scorecard is a performance measurement framework, not the internal-control framework described in the stem.
explanationSlots.EW_C: The Theory of Constraints focuses on operational bottlenecks, not entity-wide internal-control components.

P1-EC-008.assessment: Terrible distractors. This is Bloom's Remember level — all three distractors are other well-known business frameworks. Any CMA candidate who has studied internal controls for 5 minutes will recognize 'COSO' as the correct answer. Zero trap coverage. The stem is a direct definition with 'five integrated components' as the giveaway. DL-026 on EW_A. This should be scored Easy/1, not Moderate/3 per DL-031 pattern.
P1-EC-008.certification_readiness: NOT ready. Choices need redesign — too easy. DL-026 fix needed.

P1-EC-014.stem: Nightingale's internal auditors assess opportunity, pressure, and rationalization when evaluating fraud risk in a department. What model are they applying?

choices.A: The five forces model
choices.B: The fraud triangle
choices.C: The balanced scorecard
choices.D: The COSO ERM cube

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_D: COSO ERM addresses enterprise risk management broadly, but the specific three-factor fraud model in the stem is the fraud triangle.

P1-EC-014.assessment: Very weak. Stem gives away the answer with the three fraud triangle elements listed explicitly. All three distractors are frameworks from other domains — only D (COSO ERM) is even remotely in the control space. Two of three distractor explanation slots are empty (DL-026). The single non-empty slot (EW_D) is substantive. This is a definition-match item (DL-031 pattern).
P1-EC-014.certification_readiness: NOT ready. 2 DL-026 slots. Distractors need more sophistication.

P1-EC-020.stem: Thornfield stores inventory in a locked warehouse accessible only to authorized personnel with badge access. What type of control is this?

choices.A: An entity-level control unrelated to specific assets
choices.B: A detective control performed after the fact only
choices.C: A compensating control for a segregation of duties gap
choices.D: A physical control that restricts access to assets

explanationSlots.EW_B: The control is not only detective after the fact; restricted access helps prevent unauthorized physical handling or removal.
explanationSlots.EW_C: A compensating control offsets another weakness, such as limited segregation; the stem describes a direct physical access control.

P1-EC-020.assessment: Better quality. Distractors B, A, C test genuine control-type confusion (entity-level vs. detective vs. compensating vs. physical). Each represents a real concept a candidate could mistakenly apply. EW_A is empty (DL-026) — entity-level control needs explanation. EW_B and EW_C are choice-specific and substantive. Moderate overall.

P1-EC-021.topic: Segregation of duties — vendor setup and payment
P1-EC-021.stem: Bryant Manufacturing has a small accounts payable department where one employee creates new vendor records, enters invoices from those vendors, and approves payments for processing. Management wants to reduce the risk of fraudulent payments without adding staff. Which control improvement is most effective?

choices.A: Require a second employee to approve new vendor additions and review a monthly vendor-master change report
choices.B: Require the same employee to also perform the monthly bank reconciliation
choices.C: Have an internal auditor review all payments above a threshold quarterly
choices.D: Raise the dollar threshold for requiring supervisory approval of payments

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: Quarterly detective review may catch errors after the fact but does not prevent fictitious vendor payments from being initiated and approved.
explanationSlots.EW_D: Raising the threshold reduces oversight and increases, rather than decreases, the risk of unauthorized payments going undetected.

P1-EC-021.assessment: Best quality seed in Pack C Section E. Genuine business scenario with named company, realistic constraint ('without adding staff'). Distractors are clever: B makes the problem worse (same employee doing even more), C is detective-only (plausibly good but not best), D is counterproductive — exactly the type of trap that appears on the CMA exam. EW_B is empty (DL-026). Cognitive level is Apply/3 — appropriate. Strong item.

P1-EC-022.topic: Preventive vs. detective — duplicate payment control
P1-EC-022.stem: Crestview Manufacturing frequently discovers duplicate vendor payments when reviewing the monthly accounts payable aging report. Management wants to implement a control that will best prevent duplicates from occurring. Which one of the following controls is preventive?

choices.A: Require the controller to review and approve a check register weekly
choices.B: Configure the accounts payable system to reject invoices with duplicate vendor-invoice-date combinations before payment
choices.C: Perform quarterly reconciliations of vendor statements to the accounts payable subledger
choices.D: Review a monthly accounts payable aging report for unusual activity

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_D: Monthly aging report review is a detective control that identifies issues after payment has occurred, not a preventive control.

P1-EC-022.assessment: Good question testing preventive vs. detective control distinction — a core CMA Part 1 concept. A and D are both detective (common trap of confusing review/reconciliation as preventive). C is quarterly reconciliation (detective, post-payment). Company name adds realism. Two empty explanation slots (DL-026) are a significant gap. EW_D is substantive. Needs EW_A and EW_C filled.

P1-EC-023.topic: IT access control — terminated employee deprovisioning
P1-EC-023.stem: During an internal audit, Drake Distribution discovered that a former employee's system access remained active for 18 days after termination. No unauthorized transactions occurred during that period. Management wants to prevent recurrence. Which remediation is most appropriate?

choices.A: Accept the risk since no actual fraud or data loss occurred during the gap
choices.B: Require stronger password complexity standards for all system users
choices.C: Implement automated access deprovisioning triggered by termination in the HR system and require quarterly user access recertification by managers
choices.D: Convert all terminated employees to read-only access instead of removing access entirely

explanationSlots.EW_B: Stronger passwords address authentication strength but do not address the failure to revoke access for former employees in a timely manner.
explanationSlots.EW_C: (CC slot — empty ✓)

P1-EC-023.assessment: Excellent distractors — realistic remediation options. A (risk acceptance after no harm) is a common real-world rationalization. B addresses a different IT control (authentication vs. authorization). D is a half-measure that still leaves access open. Realistic scenario with '18 days' detail adding authenticity. Two of three explanation slots are empty (DL-026), which is unfortunate for such a well-designed question. Highest potential of all Pack C seeds.
P1-EC-023.certification_readiness: Needs 2 DL-026 fixes. Otherwise near-gold quality.

P1-EC-024.topic: Application input control — sales order validation
P1-EC-024.stem: Parkview Company's sales order system accepts orders with invalid customer codes, negative quantities, and missing ship-to addresses. These errors are discovered only when invoices fail to process days later. Which application control would best address this issue?

choices.A: Generate weekly exception reports for the sales manager to review and correct
choices.B: Reconcile the sales order file to the invoice register at month-end
choices.C: Require a sales supervisor to manually approve every sales order before entry
choices.D: Implement real-time field validation in the order entry system to reject entries with invalid customer codes, negative quantities, or missing ship-to addresses

explanationSlots.EW_B: Month-end reconciliation is a detective control that finds discrepancies well after orders are processed and shipped.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Manual approval of every order is inefficient and may still miss data-format errors; it does not replace field-level system validation.

P1-EC-024.assessment: Good application-control question. A/B test detective vs. preventive (recurring CMA pattern). C tests the 'manual approval as substitute for system validation' misconception. EW_A is empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C are choice-specific and substantive. Good item.

P1-EC-025.stem: Zenith Bay requires dual signatures on checks above a threshold before payment is released. Is this a preventive or detective control, and why?

choices.A: A preventive control, because it stops an unauthorized payment before it occurs
choices.B: A compensating control used only when segregation is impossible
choices.C: A corrective control, because it fixes problems after they occur
choices.D: A detective control, because it identifies errors after the fact

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: A corrective control fixes problems after they occur, while dual signatures are applied before the payment is released.
explanationSlots.EW_D: A detective control identifies errors after the fact; this control is timed before disbursement and is designed to prevent improper payment.

P1-EC-025.assessment: Good core concept (preventive vs. detective). B tests a related control classification. C and D test the same misconception (detective/corrective = after-the-fact). Distractors are moderately similar in how they test the same error. EW_B is empty (DL-026). EW_C and EW_D are substantive. Below EC-021 in quality but adequate for the topic.

P1-EC-028.stem: Copperline has a designated employee, independent of cash handling and recording, perform the monthly bank reconciliation. Why is independence important here?

choices.A: It guarantees no bank fees will ever be charged
choices.B: It removes the need for management review of cash balances
choices.C: It eliminates the need to compare the bank statement to the general ledger
choices.D: It ensures the reconciliation can objectively detect errors or irregularities without being influenced by the preparer's own transactions

explanationSlots.EW_B: Management review may still be needed; independence strengthens, but does not eliminate, oversight of cash balances.
explanationSlots.EW_C: The reconciliation still requires comparing bank records to accounting records; independence does not remove that step.

P1-EC-028.assessment: Weak distractors. A is obviously wrong (no control guarantees anything). C is definitionally wrong (eliminates need to compare — of course you still need to compare). B is the only reasonably plausible one. EW_A empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C substantive. The correct answer is also the longest choice by far (length cueing).
P1-EC-028.certification_readiness: Needs DL-026 fix + choice A redesign. Below threshold for quality.

P1-EC-031.stem: Foxglove's board defines the amount of risk the organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives. What enterprise risk management concept is being defined?

choices.A: Risk transfer
choices.B: Inherent risk
choices.C: Risk appetite
choices.D: Control risk

explanationSlots.EW_B: Inherent risk is the susceptibility of an assertion to material misstatement before considering controls. Risk appetite is the amount of risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its objectives — a strategic governance concept.
explanationSlots.EW_C: (CC slot — empty ✓)

P1-EC-031.assessment: Definition-match item (DL-031 pattern). Stem is a direct definition of risk appetite. Two of three explanation slots empty (DL-026). EW_B is very good (distinguishes inherent risk from risk appetite) but buried alone. A and D are weak — risk transfer and control risk are clearly not the definition of 'amount of risk willing to accept'.
P1-EC-031.certification_readiness: Needs 2 DL-026 fixes + distractor improvement. Marginally acceptable.

P1-EC-040.topic: IT general controls — logical access review
P1-EC-040.stem: Oleander requires periodic review of user access rights to ensure employees only retain system access appropriate to their current role. What category of control is this?

choices.A: An application control embedded in transaction processing only
choices.B: A budgetary control over IT spending
choices.C: A physical control over the data center only
choices.D: An IT general control over logical access

explanationSlots.EW_B: A budgetary control over IT spending does not validate whether users have appropriate system permissions.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Physical data-center controls restrict physical entry; the stem concerns logical access rights inside systems.

P1-EC-040.assessment: Good IT control classification question. A tests application vs. general (key CMA distinction). B tests budget vs. logical control. C tests physical vs. logical. All three test different control-type confusions. EW_A empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C are choice-specific. Decent quality.

P1-EC-041.stem: Pinehollow's CEO instructs the controller to bypass a normal approval control to record a favorable adjusting entry near year-end. What internal control limitation does this illustrate?

choices.A: Management override of controls
choices.B: Segregation of duties working exactly as designed
choices.C: An IT general control weakness
choices.D: A cost-benefit limitation of control design

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: The facts describe a human override of approval controls, not a logical-access or other IT general-control weakness.
explanationSlots.EW_D: Cost-benefit limitations concern whether a control is worth implementing; the issue here is intentional bypass of an existing control.

P1-EC-041.assessment: Strong item with realistic CEO-controller override scenario. B is clever (funny/distractor — segregation working 'as designed' when someone is bypassing it). C and D test genuine alternative control limitations. EW_B empty (DL-026) — unfortunately the most interesting distractor has no explanation. EW_C and EW_D substantive. Cognitive level Apply/3 appropriate.
P1-EC-041.certification_readiness: Needs DL-026 fix (EW_B). Otherwise very good.

P1-EC-049.stem: Yorkshire establishes an anonymous reporting channel for employees to report suspected fraud or ethical violations without fear of retaliation. What internal control objective does this serve?

choices.A: Encouraging detection and reporting of fraud or misconduct that might otherwise go unreported
choices.B: Guaranteeing that no fraud will ever occur
choices.C: Replacing the need for a code of conduct
choices.D: Eliminating the need for an external audit

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: A hotline complements a code of conduct; it does not replace the need for standards of ethical behavior.
explanationSlots.EW_D: External audits may still be required or useful; an internal reporting channel does not eliminate independent audit work.

P1-EC-049.assessment: Adequate. B is obviously wrong (no control 'guarantees' anything — absolute language trap). C and D are plausible overstatements. EW_B empty (DL-026). EW_C and EW_D substantive. Not as strong as EC-041 or EC-021 but serviceable.

P1-EC-052.stem: Cliffside is too small to fully segregate duties among its few accounting employees. What can help mitigate this control weakness?

choices.A: Ignoring the risk since fraud is unlikely in small companies
choices.B: Outsourcing all accounting with no oversight
choices.C: Eliminating internal controls entirely since the company is small
choices.D: Increased owner or management review and oversight as a compensating control

explanationSlots.EW_B: Outsourcing without oversight does not remove management responsibility or ensure controls are operating.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Small companies still need internal controls; the issue is designing practical compensating controls.

P1-EC-052.assessment: Important topic (small business compensating controls). A and C are overtly bad advice (should be obvious to anyone with basic controls training). B is more nuanced — outsourcing is a real option but 'with no oversight' makes it clearly wrong. EW_A empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C substantive. Acceptable but not strong.

P1-EC-060.topic: Control environment — tone at the top
P1-EC-060.stem: Knollwood's board and senior executives consistently emphasize integrity and ethical behavior, which shapes employee attitudes toward compliance. What COSO component does this describe?

choices.A: Monitoring activities, which evaluate control effectiveness over time
choices.B: Risk assessment, which identifies specific threats
choices.C: Information and communication, which relays data throughout the entity
choices.D: The control environment, often summarized as tone at the top

explanationSlots.EW_B: Risk assessment identifies and analyzes specific threats; tone at the top is part of the control environment.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Information and communication concerns how relevant information is captured and shared; the stem describes ethical leadership and culture.

P1-EC-060.assessment: Acceptable COSO component identification. The three distractors are the other COSO components — this tests whether the candidate can distinguish control environment from the others. EW_A empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C are substantive. Cognitive level Understand/2. The correct answer explicitly mentions 'tone at the top' which makes this very easy for prepared candidates.

P1-EC-061.stem: Lanternwood's auditor assesses the susceptibility of an account to material misstatement before considering any related controls. What type of risk is being assessed?

choices.A: Inherent risk
choices.B: Detection risk
choices.C: Control risk
choices.D: Business risk

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: Control risk considers whether controls fail to prevent or detect misstatement; the stem excludes controls from the assessment.
explanationSlots.EW_D: Business risk is broader operating or strategic risk, not the audit-risk component tied to assertion susceptibility.

P1-EC-061.assessment: Tests a key audit risk distinction. Control risk (C) is the strongest distractor — many candidates confuse inherent/control risk. Detection risk (B) and business risk (D) are less directly related but still plausible. EW_B empty (DL-026). EW_C and EW_D substantive. The stem explicitly says 'before considering controls' which essentially gives away the answer.

P1-EC-066.topic: Segregation of duties — cash custody and recording
P1-EC-066.stem: Quailrun has the same employee both handling incoming cash receipts and recording them in the accounting records. What control weakness does this create?

choices.A: A physical access control weakness only
choices.B: A lack of segregation of duties between asset custody and recordkeeping, increasing the risk of concealed theft or errors
choices.C: An IT general control deficiency only
choices.D: An overly strong control environment with too many checks

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_D: The control environment is not overly strong; the described arrangement weakens control by enabling concealment.

P1-EC-066.assessment: Classic segregation of duties question but distractors are weak. A and C are 'only' qualifiers that should be obvious. D is sarcastic/funny — 'overly strong with too many checks' when the scenario describes a clear weakness. Two explanation slots empty (DL-026). EW_D is the only non-empty slot and it's decent. Should be scored Easy/1 per DL-031.
P1-EC-066.certification_readiness: Needs 2 DL-026 fixes. Distractors need improvement.

P1-EC-072.stem: Willowmere identifies a control deficiency during its internal control assessment and assigns an owner, a corrective action plan, and a target completion date. What internal control process is being followed?

choices.A: External audit sign-off, which requires no internal follow-up
choices.B: Control environment assessment, which is unrelated to specific deficiencies
choices.C: Risk acceptance, which tolerates the deficiency permanently
choices.D: Remediation tracking, ensuring identified deficiencies are corrected and verified

explanationSlots.EW_B: Control environment assessment is broad and entity-level; the stem describes tracking a specific deficiency through correction.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Risk acceptance would tolerate the deficiency; assigning a corrective plan and deadline shows remediation, not acceptance.

P1-EC-072.assessment: Good topic (remediation tracking as a monitoring subprocess). A is obviously wrong (external audit doesn't do remediation). B and C test confusion with other COSO concepts. EW_A empty (DL-026). EW_B and EW_C substantive. Acceptable quality.

P1-ED-001.stem: Bramblewood structures its risk and control functions using operational management, risk/compliance oversight, and internal audit as distinct layers. What model is this?

choices.A: The COSO ERM cube alone
choices.B: The three lines of defense (or three lines) model
choices.C: The fraud triangle
choices.D: The balanced scorecard

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: The balanced scorecard is a performance measurement tool, not a governance model for control responsibilities.
explanationSlots.EW_D: COSO ERM is broader risk-management guidance; the distinct operational, oversight, and internal-audit layers describe the three lines model.

P1-ED-001.assessment: Definition-match (DL-031). Stem explicitly describes the three lines. Distractors are all unrelated frameworks. Only D (COSO ERM) is in the same governance space. EW_B correctly empty. Two slots empty (EW_A + 1 more — DL-026). EW_C misattributes control to 'balanced scorecard' description for the fraud triangle slot — possible DL-016 metadata-content shift.
P1-ED-001.certification_readiness: NOT ready. Distractors need redesign. DL-026 fixes needed.

P1-ED-010.topic: Access control — principle of least privilege
P1-ED-010.stem: Fernhollow grants employees system access limited only to what is necessary to perform their specific job duties. What security principle is being applied?

choices.A: Risk transfer
choices.B: The principle of least privilege
choices.C: Management override
choices.D: The principle of maximum access for efficiency

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_D: Management override is bypassing controls, not a principle for limiting user access.

P1-ED-010.assessment: Very weak. Definition-match item. D is humorous/funny (maximum access for efficiency — opposite of the described practice). A and C are unrelated concepts. Two empty explanation slots (DL-026). EW_D is the only substantive slot. Should be Easy/1.

P1-ED-014.stem: Northfell has a supervisor recount inventory counted by warehouse staff before finalizing the count. What type of control activity is this?

choices.A: A physical control over inventory storage only
choices.B: Independent verification, checking the accuracy of work performed by others
choices.C: A preventive control that stops errors before they occur
choices.D: Segregation of duties, since only one person performs the recount

explanationSlots.EW_B: (CC slot — empty ✓)
explanationSlots.EW_C: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_D: Segregation of duties separates incompatible responsibilities; a one-person recount by a supervisor is independent verification, not the segregation concept itself.

P1-ED-014.assessment: Tests the critical distinction between independent verification and segregation of duties — a common CMA candidate confusion. C tests preventive vs. detective. A tests physical control. Two empty explanation slots (DL-026). Only EW_D is substantive. Labeled 'Difficult' but content doesn't justify — standard Identify/Understand.

P1-ED-016.stem: Palisade decides to purchase insurance to address a significant identified risk rather than eliminate the underlying activity. What enterprise risk management response is this?

choices.A: Risk appetite, defining the amount of risk tolerated
choices.B: Risk avoidance, eliminating the risk entirely
choices.C: Risk acceptance, taking no action
choices.D: Risk transfer (sharing), shifting some financial impact of the risk to a third party

explanationSlots.EW_B: This option reflects a misunderstanding of erm risk response strategies. The choice 'Risk avoidance, eliminating the risk entirely' is inconsistent with the correct treatment under CMA Part 1 guidelines for this topic area. Review the applicable costing standard or framework to understand why this approach is not appropriate.
explanationSlots.EW_C: This option reflects a misunderstanding of erm risk response strategies. The choice 'Risk acceptance, taking no action' is inconsistent with the correct treatment under CMA Part 1 guidelines for this topic area. Review the applicable costing standard or framework to understand why this approach is not appropriate.

P1-ED-016.assessment: Good choices — all three distractors are actual ERM response strategies. However, explanation quality is POOR: EW_B and EW_C use generic template text ('This option reflects a misunderstanding... Review the applicable costing standard...'). These are DL-013 boilerplate variants that provide ZERO educational value. A learner choosing B or C learns nothing specific. EW_A is empty (DL-026). Three distinct explanation quality issues.
P1-ED-016.certification_readiness: NOT ready. EW_B and EW_C need genuine choice-specific text. EW_A needs DL-026 fix.

P1-ED-025.stem: Zionsgate requires that all purchase orders above a certain dollar amount be approved by a manager before the order is placed. What type of control activity is this?

choices.A: An authorization control
choices.B: A monitoring activity performed after the fact
choices.C: A segregation of duties control only
choices.D: A risk assessment activity

explanationSlots.EW_B: (DL-026: empty slot)
explanationSlots.EW_C: Segregation may support purchasing controls, but the specific activity described is management authorization.
explanationSlots.EW_D: Risk assessment identifies and analyzes risk; it is not the transaction-level approval control described.

P1-ED-025.assessment: Good authorization control question. B tests control activity vs. monitoring component. C tests the common SoD vs. authorization confusion. D tests COSO component misidentification. EW_B empty (DL-026). EW_C and EW_D are substantive. Solid for an authorization control item.

P1-ED-028.stem: Crownridge's management periodically reviews exception reports and reconciliations as part of regular operations to assess whether controls are functioning as intended. What COSO component does this represent?

choices.A: Risk assessment
choices.B: Information and communication
choices.C: Control environment
choices.D: Monitoring activities

explanationSlots.EW_B: Information and communication supports reporting relevant information, but the periodic review of exceptions and reconciliations is monitoring.
explanationSlots.EW_C: Control environment concerns tone, structure, and accountability; the stem focuses on evaluating whether controls continue to operate.

P1-ED-028.assessment: One of the better Pack D seeds. All three distractors are the other COSO components, forcing genuine component-level discrimination. Monitoring vs. information/communication is a real CMA trap. EW_A empty (DL-026) but EW_B and EW_C are substantive. Cognitive level Apply/4 (labeled Difficult) — appropriate given the component discrimination needed. Good item.

P1-ED-035.stem: Jettison maintains offsite backups of critical financial data and a documented plan for restoring systems after a disruption. What control objective does this address?

choices.A: Segregation of duties within the IT department
choices.B: Authorization controls over transaction approval
choices.C: Availability of information systems and data in the event of a disruption
choices.D: Confidentiality of customer data only

explanationSlots.EW_B: Transaction authorization controls approve business transactions; they do not restore systems after an outage.
explanationSlots.EW_C: (CC slot — empty ✓)

P1-ED-035.assessment: Tests the CIA triad distinction (availability vs. confidentiality). D tests confidentiality — the key distinction. A/B are weaker distractors (SoD, authorization unrelated to backups). Two empty slots (DL-026 + EW_B the only substantive). Labeled 'Difficult' but content is straightforward Understand.

P1-ED-036.stem: Kirkwood requires all software changes to be tested, approved, and documented before being moved into the production environment. What type of control is this?

choices.A: A segregation of duties control unrelated to IT
choices.B: An application control embedded in a specific transaction
choices.C: A physical control over hardware only
choices.D: An IT general control over change management

explanationSlots.EW_B: This option reflects a misunderstanding of change management control it systems. crossPoolComparison.packC_vs_packD: Pack C seeds are marginally better (mean 33.0 vs. 30.8). Pack C has 2 Tier A items (≥45) vs. 0 for Pack D. Both packs have 3 Tier D items (<25). The quality range is wider in Pack C (14-48) than Pack D (19-42).
crossPoolComparison.packD_has_more_boilerplate: Pack D seeds disproportionately use generic 'This option reflects a misunderstanding...' template text in explanations (ED-016, ED-036, ED-046, ED-051) — a DL-013 variant that provides zero educational value. Pack C seeds generally have better (if incomplete) explanation text.
crossPoolComparison.packC_explanations_stronger: When Pack C seeds have explanation text, it's typically genuine and choice-specific. When Pack D seeds have text, it's more likely to be boilerplate.

commonIssues.dl031_definition_match_inflation: ~12 of 38 seeds (32%) follow the DL-031 pattern where the stem is a direct definition and the correct answer is the term. These items should be labeled Easy (1), not Moderate (3).
commonIssues.dl026_prevalence: 94% of seeds (36/38) have at least one empty non-CC ExplanationWrong slot. 38 total empty slots across the 38 seeds — roughly 1 per item on average.
commonIssues.rotation_group_quality_ceiling: The 5-item rotation group format creates a quality ceiling: all distractors are confined to the same 4 concepts per group, shared across 5 company-name variants. This limits the range of misconceptions tested.
commonIssues.absolute_language_in_distractors: Several items use 'only,' 'entirely,' 'no,' 'eliminates' in distractors — these are obvious cueing indicators (DL-004 pattern) that make elimination trivial.
commonIssues.length_cueing: Several items have the correct answer as the longest choice text (EC-028, EC-023) — a documented psychometric bias (CAQS §6.4).

Rewrite 4 Pack D seeds with boilerplate explanations (ED-016, ED-036, ED-046, ED-051)
Redesign EC-008 and ED-010 — distractors are non-functional for any prepared candidate
short_term: Recalibrate ~12 DL-031 definition-match items from Moderate (3) → Easy (1)
Normalize answer choice lengths to eliminate length cueing
Consider breaking the 5-item rotation group pattern for 5-8 of the strongest topics to create genuinely variant distractors
long_term: Develop a Domain E distractor bank with 15-20 documented CMA exam traps mapped to specific COSO/control concepts
Implement per-distractor misconception tracking so automated tools can verify choice-specific explanation text
Replace the template-based authoring pipeline for Domain E with concept-driven authoring to improve distractor quality at source

verdict: The 38 Domain E seeds contain structurally sound choices testing relevant COSO/internal controls concepts. However, distractor quality is undermined by three systemic defects: (1) widespread DL-026 empty explanation slots (94% of seeds affected), (2) DL-013 boilerplate explanation text in Pack D seeds, and (3) DL-031 definition-match pattern making ~32% of items trivially easy despite Moderate difficulty labels. NO seed is certification-ready in its current state. All require at minimum DL-026 fixes; 8 seeds require major distractor redesign. The best items (EC-021, EC-023, ED-073) demonstrate that Domain E can produce exam-quality distractors — they just need complete explanation coverage.
